rationales: Margulis and Schwartz developed a later version of the kingdom classification, not the original five-kingdom system.
Robert Whittaker introduced the five-kingdom system in 1969.
John Ray contributed to early biological classification but did not introduce the five-kingdom system.
Ernst Haeckel proposed a three-kingdom system, not the five-kingdom system.
Telophase reverses many events of prophase, including chromosome condensation and nuclear-envelope breakdown.
Metaphase is the stage when chromosomes align at the cell’s equator.
Anaphase is the stage when sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles.
Anaphase I separates homologous chromosomes during meiosis, rather than being reversed by telophase.
The typical prokaryotic chromosome is not described as DNA combined with the histone proteins characteristic of eukaryotic chromosomes.
In the textbook description, a prokaryotic chromosome consists of DNA without histones.
Protein alone cannot carry the chromosome’s genetic information.
Lipids are not the material of a prokaryotic chromosome.
A theory may help explain laws, but it does not keep suggesting new laws in this statement.
Deduction is a way of reasoning from premises, not the new item suggested by a theory.
Observations provide evidence for theories, rather than being the intended product suggested here.
A productive theory suggests new hypotheses that can be tested.
Oscar Hertwig is credited with discovering meiosis while studying the formation of gametes.
Golgi is associated with discovery of the Golgi apparatus, not meiosis.
John Ray was a naturalist and taxonomist, not the discoverer of meiosis.
Walther Flemming described mitosis, not the discovery of meiosis.
The Greek root of metabolism does not mean “smaller.”
Metabolism comes from a Greek word meaning “change.”
“Growth” is not the meaning of the Greek word from which metabolism is derived.
“Energy” is not the literal meaning of the Greek word from which metabolism is derived.
The endodermis is a layer around the cortex, not the layer immediately outside conducting tissues.
The pericycle is the narrow cell layer just outside the vascular conducting tissues.
The cortex lies farther outward and is not the narrow layer immediately surrounding the conducting tissues.
The epidermis is the outermost protective layer, not the layer directly outside the conducting tissues.
Mitochondria are not primarily responsible for lipid storage.
Protein synthesis occurs mainly on ribosomes.
Photosynthesis takes place in chloroplasts, not mitochondria.
Mitochondria carry out cellular respiration and produce much of the cell’s ATP.
ATP was not discovered in 1939.
ATP was not discovered in 1941.
ATP was not discovered in 1949.
ATP was discovered in 1929 by Karl Lohmann.
The organism level is identifiable in plants as the whole plant.
Plant organs such as roots, stems, and leaves are clearly recognizable.
The organ-system level is less clearly defined in plants than in animals.
Tissues are recognizable levels of organization in plants.
Interphase occupies at least about 90% of the cell cycle.
Karyokinesis is a comparatively short stage of cell division.
Cytokinesis is a comparatively short stage of cell division.
Prophase is one part of mitosis and does not occupy 90% of the whole cell cycle.
Édouard Chatton introduced the terms prokaryotic and eukaryotic.
Robert Whittaker is known for introducing the five-kingdom classification.
Ernst Haeckel proposed a three-kingdom classification.
Margulis contributed to later work on classification and cell evolution, but did not first suggest these terms.
Vitamin A is associated with sources such as liver and green vegetables, but citrus fruits are not its characteristic source here.
Vitamin B is not the vitamin class indicated by this combination of sources.
Citrus fruits and green vegetables are common sources of vitamin C, and liver can also contain it.
Vitamin D is chiefly associated with sunlight and certain animal foods, not this source list.
Spindle fibres do not form during telophase; they disassemble then.
The spindle begins forming during prophase.
In metaphase, the spindle is already formed and chromosomes are aligned.
In anaphase, spindle fibres pull chromatids toward opposite poles.
A male typically has about 5–5.5 million red blood cells per cubic millimeter of blood.
The range 4–4.5 million is below the usual male range given in the textbook.
The range 6–6.5 million is above the usual male range.
The range 7–7.5 million is far above the usual male range.
